whatTheyArgued: Nominated name, no author's work claimed. The compendium assigns registers to Eastwood (economy), Kubrick (precision), Strunk & White (plain style) and Terry Gross (drawing the guest out). Only Strunk & White wrote a style doctrine; Eastwood, Kubrick and Gross are credited for reputations/methods per compendium entries, which I did not independently verify.
ourUse: A closed table REGISTERS of declared sentence frames; a regex on the prompt (e.g. /plain|simply|clearly|readable|explain/) picks the register. No readability grade or Strunk & White rule is computed, though the header says 'readability grade plus the classic style rules'.

bends.ours: plain register credited as 'readability plus the classic style rules: Strunk & White'.
bends.theirs: Strunk & White give rules of composition (omit needless words, etc.) applied to prose a writer composes. The code selects a fixed frame by keyword; no rule is applied or checked.

bends.ours: Eastwood = lean, Kubrick = precise, Gross = oral, as 'archons' that 'own' a register.
bends.theirs: These are reputations of a director, a director and an interviewer, not stated doctrines of sentence framing; the frames are ours (e.g. 'It is told that X —act→ Y').

bends.ours: credit line: 'lean by Eastwood, precise by Kubrick, plain by Strunk & White, oral by Terry Gross'.
bends.theirs: None of them selected or authorized these frames; the mapping is a project choice.

noBendReason: Name 'output-voice / The Register' and the frame table are ours and claim no author's work; the bends concern the four borrowed credits.
fix: compendium work: 'A register is a closed set of DECLARED frames, the only words beyond the claim's own (as compose.js TRANSITIONS are declared token origins). The prompt's cues pick the register; the words never do. Register names echo Eastwood, Kubrick, Strunk & White and Terry Gross by analogy; none of their methods is implemented.'
credit: 'The register (output-voice) — our name: a closed set of declared frames chosen by prompt cues, never an invented sentence.'
